title: [CQ-RF03] Replace an unverified running daemon
description:
Objective: when a protected project finds a running daemon whose provenance does not verify, the IDE can stop it with the INSTALLED CLI's `stop` and start its own installed daemon, rather than only refusing. A daemon that VS Code shares is never stopped without asking. This is CQ-R01 follow-up 3.

Created by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30, when the human moved the non-gating R01 follow-ups out of CQ-R13. It edits MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt after CQ-RF01.

Deliverable: MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt.
- On an unverified daemon, run the installed daemon CLI's `stop --project <path>`, never a repository binary.
- Wait, within a fixed bound, for the daemon to exit and daemon.json to clear.
- Then spawn the installed daemon with fresh provenance.
- If another client is registered on that daemon, ask first through an injectable confirmer.
- A failed or timed-out stop keeps today's refusal.
- Tests in MoeDaemonSupervisorTest use an injected process runner.

Out of scope:
- CQ-RF01, RF02 and RF04;
- VS Code changes;
- .moe edits;
- enabling verified-local.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"
definitionOfDone: An unverified running daemon is stopped only through the installed CLI's stop command, and the installed daemon is then started with fresh provenance. Shown by tests with an injected process runner.
A daemon with another registered client is never stopped without explicit confirmation, and a failed or timed-out stop leaves today's refusal in place. Shown by tests.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt: replace an unverified daemon inside ensureDaemonRunning().

In the branch where daemon.json's daemon is alive and listening, call replacedUnverified(info) before the early return. A false answer returns false exactly as today. A true answer falls through to the existing stale-file cleanup and spawn.

replacedUnverified(info) answers false, and does nothing, unless ALL of these hold, checked in order:
1. The profile is PROTECTED, activationRefusal(info) is non-null, and the caller is not on the EDT (onDispatchThread false). The EDT never prompts or waits: project open connects there, and the tool window's pooled connect() makes the attempt.
2. No other replacement is in flight: an AtomicBoolean, compareAndSet.
3. stopCommandOrNull(basePath) is non-null.
4. Before anything is stopped, capture target = processLookup(info.pid) and parent = target.parent(). A null target means false.
5. replaceConfirmer(projectName, info.pid) answers true. A throw is false.
   - The confirmer is ALWAYS asked. The IDE cannot learn whether another client (VS Code, a terminal agent) shares an unverified daemon from anything it can trust. That daemon's own report would be caller-minted evidence, which the epic rails forbid using to skip a human check.
6. runStop(stopBuilder) answers exactly 0. A null (timed out) or non-zero answer is false.
7. Within EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS, polling every POLL_MS through sleep, all of these become true:
   - target is not alive;
   - parent is null or not alive;
   - daemon.json is absent, or names a pid that isProcessAlive denies.
   Waiting for the parent closes the old-supervisor race: a new supervisor consumes the stop sentinel when it starts, so an old supervisor that is still alive could respawn its child. If the bound runs out, the answer is false.

On true: log at info level, resetSpawnBackoff() so the cooldown cannot strand the project, and fall through. The installed daemon then starts with fresh provenance (recordProtectedSpawn, persisted by RF01).

On any false after the confirmation:
- Keep today's refusal, with its exact text.
- If the stop removed daemon.json while target is still alive, set selectionRefusal to that same refusal text, so connect() shows it instead of 'Daemon not running', and spawn nothing while that captured target lives.
- Log the failing condition at warn level.

Error handling:
- replacedUnverified never throws: any exception is false, and is logged.
- The flag is released in finally.
- No process is signalled except through the installed CLI's stop.
- Restart Daemon (stopDaemonForRestart) is unchanged; RF04 owns it.
implementationPlan.note: Integrated confirmed installed-CLI stop, captured target/parent, bounded wait and fresh provenance spawn. Safety adjustment within same scope: the AtomicBoolean protects the entire protected ensure call through fall-through spawn (not only replacedUnverified), closing concurrent missing-metadata duplicate-start races. Retained captured target AND parent across retries prevents bypass after stop removes metadata. Pure bounded metadata reread avoids readDaemonInfo's known deleting/null-on-error semantics; malformed/unreadable metadata is not clearance. LEGACY body and stopDaemonForRestart unchanged. GREEN remains step 5.

implementationPlan.description:
MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt: the production replaceConfirmer, a small private function in the same file.

- With ApplicationManager.getApplication() null, in unit-test mode or headless: answer false and show nothing.
- Otherwise, on the calling (pooled) thread, run invokeAndWait on the EDT with Messages.showDialog:
  - options ["Keep It", "Stop and Replace"], with "Keep It" (0) as the default;
  - title "Moe: Unverified Daemon";
  - the message: "The daemon that .moe/daemon.json names for <projectName> (pid N) was not started by this IDE from the installed Moe runtime. Another client, such as VS Code or a terminal agent, may be using it, and stopping it disconnects them. Stop it with the installed Moe CLI and start the installed daemon?"
  It answers true only for choice 1. Escape or closing the dialog returns -1, which answers false.
- The pid comes from repository content, so the text never asserts that the process IS a Moe daemon. The installed CLI's stop validates it (pid and project through /health) before signalling anything.

Error handling: any exception (an interrupted invokeAndWait, a disposed application) is logged and answers false.
implementationPlan.note: Production confirmation now invokes the exact safe-default Keep It / Stop and Replace dialog on EDT from pooled callers; only choice 1 consents. Null application, unit-test/headless mode, direct EDT calls, exceptions and interruption fail closed (interrupt status restored). RP5 exercises default no-application behavior; dialog copy avoids trusting repository pid. No restart behavior touched.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the two-file diff as an attacker:
- Can any process be signalled without an explicit 'Stop and Replace': a throw, Escape, a headless IDE, or the EDT?
- Can the stop ever run a repository or PATH binary, or inherit NODE_OPTIONS or NODE_PATH, or the project as its working directory?
- After a failed or timed-out stop, can anything start a daemon while the old target lives, or show a weaker message than today's refusal?
- Can the wait run unbounded, or block the EDT? Can two replacements overlap?
- Can a respawn by the old supervisor race the new start? (The parent wait.)
- Is LEGACY byte-for-byte unchanged? Is a verified daemon still activated without a prompt?
- daemon.json is repository content: does its pid reach anything but the confirmer's text and the captured handle?
- Would I be embarrassed if this shipped?

Fix any finding, then re-run step 5's command fresh before complete_task.

comments.content:
architect-4ae016fb, 2026-10-30: three notes for this row's worker. I agreed them in #architects with RF04's architect (architect-e4b7eee0).

1. `--host` once task-0c72d59a lands. This row now dependsOn 0c72d59a, a HIGH security fix: JetBrains WSL agent mode starts the daemon with `--host wsl` instead of `--host 0.0.0.0`.
   - Where steps 1 and 2 say "--host 0.0.0.0", read it as "the WSL host that protectedDaemonCommand produces in the landed bytes".
   - Keep 0c72d59a's constant, and never write 0.0.0.0 back.
   - RP1 asserts the landed value on 'start'. 'stop' never carries --host.

2. On Windows, the stop leaves daemon.json behind. There, Node's process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM') is TerminateProcess, so `_run`'s shutdown cleanup never runs. After a successful stop, daemon.json usually still names the now-dead pid.
   - Step 3's condition "daemon.json absent, or names a pid that isProcessAlive denies" is deliberate. Do not narrow it to "absent".
   - RP1's fake stop deletes the file, so add one RP1 variant that pins the Windows shape. runStop returns 0; target and parent die, processAliveProbe included; daemon.json stays in place, naming 4242.
   - Expected: the replacement proceeds, the existing stale cleanup removes the file, and processStarter runs the installed start once.

3. stopCommandOrNull has no side effect apart from its warn log. RF04 (task-de91373a) also calls it from the Windows Restart Daemon path under LEGACY, and treats null as a failed stop.
   - On a Refused selection it neither calls onStatus nor sets selectionRefusal; those stay with protectedCommandOrRefuse.
   - Node resolves exactly as in protectedCommandOrRefuse: the nodeExecutable seam, else resolveNodeExecutable with nodeOnProtectedPath. Share that resolution rather than copying it.
   - RF04's plan cites stopCommandOrNull, runStop, sleep, EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS and POLL_MS by name, so keep those names.

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
Amendment to comment-08300e67, point 3 (architect-4ae016fb, 2026-10-30). Agreed in #architects with RF04's architect (architect-e4b7eee0, msg-4599ebde). Point 3 covered only the Refused case. This is the full contract.

stopCommandOrNull(basePath)'s only side effect is the warn log on a refusal.
- It never sets selectionRefusal, never clears it, and never calls onStatus, on Refused and on Ready alike.
- Step 2.3's 'leaves the refusal in place' means the field keeps what it already holds. It does not store the new refusal.
- Share only the node resolution with protectedCommandOrRefuse: the nodeExecutable seam, else resolveNodeExecutable with nodeOnProtectedPath. Never call protectedCommandOrRefuse itself. It clears the field on Ready (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:243), and on Refused it sets the field and calls onStatus (:246-248).
- Unchanged: step 3's own write in replacedUnverified, when the stop removed daemon.json while the captured target lives, stays as planned. Condition 1 makes it PROTECTED-only.

Why:
- RF04 (task-de91373a) calls stopCommandOrNull on the LEGACY Windows restart path, where null means a failed stop.
- A stored refusal there would publish a 'Protected execution profile: …' status under LEGACY. It would also come back once the project switched to PROTECTED, because only selectionRefusal()'s PROTECTED filter (:166) hides it.
- If it cleared the field on Ready, a live refusal would be erased, and connect() would show 'Daemon not running' instead.

Add one row to step 1, RP-S, so a violation fails here and not later in RF04's W4(d). Call stopCommandOrNull directly; `internal` visibility, like protectedDaemonEnvironment, is fine.
- (a) LEGACY, node unresolvable (nodeExecutable answers null). Expect: it returns null, onStatus records no call, and selectionRefusal() is null. It must stay null after the test flips its profile seam to PROTECTED.
- (b) PROTECTED with a refusal already stored by a refused start, e.g. ensureDaemonRunning() with daemon.json absent and node unresolvable. Then make node resolve. Expect: stopCommandOrNull returns the installed `stop --project <basePath>` command (no --host), selectionRefusal() still returns the earlier refusal, and onStatus gains no call.
- Mutant for the adversarial pass: routing stopCommandOrNull through protectedCommandOrRefuse must fail (a) and (b).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Asking only when the daemon reports other clients. Rejected:
  - /health has no client count, and adding one is a daemon protocol change outside this row.
  - More importantly, anything an unverified daemon reports is caller-minted. Using it to skip the human check is what the epic rail forbids.
  - So the confirmer is always asked. That satisfies DoD 2 as a superset, and the replacement still beats today's refuse-only behaviour.
- Replacing on the EDT. Rejected: projectOpened runs connect() on the EDT, and a confirm-stop-wait sequence of up to ~35 s would freeze the UI. The tool window's pooled connect() does it instead.
- Signalling the pid from the IDE. Rejected: the task requires the installed CLI's stop, which validates pid and project through /health and writes the stop sentinel.
- Waiting only for the daemon. Rejected, because of the old-supervisor race: superviseDaemon consumes the stop sentinel at startup, so an old supervisor that is still alive could respawn. The wait also covers the daemon's direct parent.
- Remembering declines. Rejected: every explicit connect may ask again, so the user can change their mind. The in-flight flag stops overlapping prompts.
- An async confirmer like RF02's. Rejected: the stop needs the answer first, and a pooled thread may block on invokeAndWait.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- MoeProjectService.connect() calls ensureDaemonRunning() and then doConnect(), which publishes activationRefusal with no retry.
  - MoeProjectOpenListener.projectOpened calls connect() on the EDT.
  - MoeToolWindowPanel:360 calls it through executeOnPooledThread.
- ensureDaemonRunning returns false early for a live daemon. Below that branch it cleans stale files and spawns under the spawn-attempt cap and the 10 s cooldown (resetSpawnBackoff resets both).
- protectedDaemonCommand builds [node, daemon, 'start', '--project', basePath] from installedArtifact and installedExecutable, plus --host for WSL agents. protectedDaemonEnvironment strips NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH and filters PATH.
- The daemon CLI's stopDaemon (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:996):
  - it validates daemon.json through validateDaemonInfoForProject (pid alive plus probeDaemonHealth);
  - it writes the stop sentinel, then sends SIGTERM;
  - an invalid file is cleaned up without any signal, still with exit 0.
- superviseDaemon consumes the sentinel at startup (index.ts:885) and on child exit (index.ts:918).
- processLookup's ProcessHandle checks the start time, so a captured handle is immune to pid reuse.
planningNotes.risks:
- Assumed interface: RF01's recordProtectedSpawn(basePath, process, installedDaemon) and activationRefusal(info) passing installedDaemon to verifyProvenance. Adapt to the landed signatures.
- If the tool window never initializes, the EDT connect keeps today's refusal until the user opens the tool window.
- The installed CLI's stop exits 0 even when it only cleaned up an invalid daemon.json without signalling. The bounded wait then fails, and selectionRefusal keeps the refusal visible while the captured target lives.
- On Windows, SIGTERM is TerminateProcess, so daemon.json can outlive its pid. A file that names a dead pid counts as clear, and the existing stale cleanup removes it.
- Restart Daemon (stopDaemonForRestart) is unchanged; CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a) owns the restart race and depends on this row.
- This plan touches only MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt and MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt, which are file-disjoint from RF02, so RF02 is dropped from dependsOn.
- Kotlin gate: Windows gradlew.bat through cmd.exe, under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

completionSummary:
Implemented protected unverified-daemon replacement with explicit safe-default confirmation, installed CLI stop, sanitized environment/cwd, bounded stop and captured target/parent exit wait, and installed restart with fresh persisted provenance. Start retains --host wsl; stop has no --host. Side-effect-free stopCommandOrNull shares only protected node resolution, preserving RF04 contract. Restart method untouched; legacy behavior preserved.
Atomic guard covers protected ensure through spawn. Failed replacement retains original refusal and captured identities across retries; both processes and bounded nondeleting metadata clearance must succeed before retry can spawn. Adversarial testing caught and fixed retry bypass with malformed/new-live-pid metadata.
Tests-first RED on missing seams; seven RP methods cover confirmed/declined/thrown/EDT/headless, stop failures/timeouts, target/parent/newpid/malformed metadata, Windows retained dead-pid metadata, reentry/retries, provenance, selector side effects and default CLI cleanup. Five mutants assertion-killed then restored. FINAL exact Windows Gradle command exited 0: 392 tests, zero failures/errors/skips, supervisor 30/30. Lease released; diff --check clean. Source/test +356/-11, 198 added test lines. Serena handoff/gotcha written. Only two scoped source/test files plus ignored Serena metadata modified; peer bytes preserved, no agent Git writes.
